samples_reviewed.question_text: There are 10 groups of 4 (4 added 10 times). How many in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Counting by repeated addition is directly served, with the sums written out at seeds 600, 602 and 605, and creating equal groups is genuinely asked through the shading tasks at seeds 44 and 502. What is missing is one of the two forms of language the competency explicitly names.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names two ways of talking about equal groups and only one of them is ever generated. All sixteen seeds use the groups of phrasing; not a single sample uses the plural multiple naming form, for example calling five groups of three by the name five threes. A named sub-case producing zero items is an uncovered sub-case.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Load is managed sensibly: short sums are spelled out term by term at seeds 603 and 605, while the long ones are compressed into an added so many times phrase at seeds 501 and 502 instead of printing ten addends. Sentence length and vocabulary fit the third quarter of Grade 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only seed 601 is a genuine context problem, and its baskets placed inside bags framing is both semantically backwards and structurally identical to the container stem used by the neighbouring node. Separately, all four error detect items, seeds 47, 500, 602 and 605, are keyed as no error, so that format never once asks a pupil to locate a mistake.

competency_alignment.rationale: Across seeds 43, 600, 501 and 603 the quantities that move are the number of groups and the size of each group, which is the equal grouping relationship the competency is about, rather than surface features of the question.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The upper end is well chosen, reaching 100 at seed 501 and 80 at seed 502. The floor is not: seed 61 collapses to one group of one and then presents a bare claim about 1 and 2, which exercises nothing about repeated addition and reads as a malformed item rather than an easy one.
